A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HotSpot and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The complete 24-page v1 and 26-page v2 support reliable matching despite renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original reconstruction and distance-query experiments on 2D shapes, ShapeNet, high-genus geometries, and SRB, plus ablations and sphere-tracing results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and adds ShapeNet baseline results, runtime measurements, and a 1D CP-loss experiment.

M1.justification: The signed-distance output, heat-field substitution, heat loss, and combined boundary/eikonal/heat objective remain identical in Equations 6–8. The new sufficiency framing and comparison experiments do not change HotSpot's procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover 1D examples, 14 2D shapes, the 260-shape ShapeNet subset, seven high-genus shapes, five SRB scans, and ShapeNet sphere tracing. The added CP-loss and timing comparisons remain within existing task and domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the evaluated comparison set: Neural-Singular-Hessian and Neural-Pull join the ShapeNet comparisons in Tables 7–9, corresponding to v1 Tables 6–8. Appendix B.1 also adds Marschner et al.'s CP loss to the 1D comparison. NeurCADRecon is cited but has no reported comparison row.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a controlled runtime protocol: 100 training iterations on one ShapeNet model, comparing HotSpot and StEik with four architectures combining 5 or 8 layers and 128 or 256 channels, with other settings matched. Existing reconstruction, sampling, and sphere-tracing protocols are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.1 and Figure 11 test whether CP loss excludes non-distance solutions, demonstrating collapse toward the zero function. Existing loss-combination ablations, absorption/eikonal-weight sensitivity analyses, and PHASE boundary-weight studies are retained.

E5.justification: Both appendices report dataset metrics using mean, median, and standard deviation. V2 applies the same reporting format to added baseline rows; neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing scores are retained, but v2 adds substantial comparative evidence. Neural-Pull's overall ShapeNet RMSE is 0.0093 versus HotSpot's unchanged 0.0281, while its near-surface RMSE is 0.0123 versus HotSpot's 0.0094 (Tables 8–9). New Table 4 reports faster HotSpot training across four matched architectures, and Figure 11 adds the CP-loss failure result.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 revises the coarea stationarity equation and accompanying argument. Appendix A.2 corrects the 2D solution's prefactor from exp(-lambda epsilon) to h_0e (v1 Equation 28; v2 Equation 29). Appendix B.1 adds the CP-loss zero-function counterexample. The principal convergence bound and stability proofs remain.

C1.justification: The asymptotic-sufficiency wording emphasizes the bounded convergence already claimed in v1. Both versions retain the same central contributions: convergence toward true distance, spatial and temporal stability, compatible surface-area regularization, and improved reconstruction and distance approximation.

C2.justification: V2 adds an efficiency explanation based on first-order versus second-order derivatives and expands the interpretation of closest-point methods' near-surface errors. Appendix B.3 changes the overall distance-accuracy characterization from best to near-top. Existing numerical-precision, sparse-boundary, and unsigned-collapse limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies a single NVIDIA A10 GPU and reports training times for four network configurations in Section 6 and Table 4. Existing architecture, sampling, scheduling, and sphere-tracing details remain; detailed training configurations for the newly added ShapeNet baselines are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references, including Neural-Singular-Hessian, Neural-Pull, NeurCADRecon, GridPull, Neural Poisson, Shape as Points, and Belyaev–Fayolle's 2015 work. Related work expands its discussion of higher-order constraints and closest-point methods while retaining the heat-transfer and PHASE foundations.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and revises the abstract, contribution wording, related work, and explanatory passages around necessary versus sufficient conditions. It adds an Efficiency paragraph, a 1D Verification subsection, and acknowledgements, while preserving the main section sequence and most appendix exposition.

P2.justification: V2 adds the logical diagram in Figure 2, the CP-loss comparison in Figure 11, and runtime Table 4. ShapeNet tables gain baseline rows and revised ranking formatting. Existing figures and tables are renumbered or relocated, with the original reconstruction and sensitivity graphics preserved.

improvement.justification: The added baselines better reveal HotSpot's strengths and weaknesses, while controlled timings and the CP-loss check fill limited validation gaps. The appendix prefactor correction also resolves a concrete error. These gains outweigh a remaining reporting inconsistency: Appendix B.3 retains a claim of near-surface reductions above one-third, although Table 9's RMSE advantage over Neural-Pull is about 24%.
